the presence of oestrogen receptors in breast cancer is related to the patient’s age and postmenopause, but not to other factors such as the duration of the disease, the extent of the primary tumour, the presence of axillary lymph node metastases and the histological type and grade of the tumours.
oestrogen receptor ( ER) status in breast cancer was not associated with any of the clinical and pathological factors studied, except age and postmenopause.
the oestrogen receptor content of the primary tumour was associated with increasing age and post-menopausal status but was not related to the other clinical and histopathological factors examined.

the identification of the risk factors and the clinical features associated with oestrogen receptors in breast cancer.
the relationship between age and menopausai status and the presence of oestrogen receptors.
the identification of the factors that are associated with a high probability of the presence of oestrogen receptors in the primary tumour in patients with ‘operable breast cancer’.
